summary: This work accelerates logical operations in quantum LDPC codes by combining cat-state-based measurements of multiple commuting Pauli operators using scheduler codes, achieving 3× speedup for joint logical measurements and up to 74× speedup for random Clifford circuits when integrated with a modified CliNR scheme. The approach is demonstrated numerically on the Q70 and Q102 codes from the walking cat architecture with measurement flip rate $p_F = 6.3 \times 10^{-3}$ and target error rate $\varepsilon = 10^{-10}$.
motivation: Quantum LDPC codes offer high encoding rates and qubit efficiency compared to surface codes, but simultaneous logical operations on multiple qubits within the same block are slow because prior work requires complex resource states for logical measurements.
method: The authors generalize Shor's cat-based measurement scheme to jointly measure $\ell$ commuting logical Pauli operators using an $\ell \times m$ scheduler code (a binary linear code) that specifies the measurement sequence and enables decoding of all outcomes. They develop error-detected (MEDM) and error-corrected (MECM) variants that terminate early when sufficient confidence is reached, and combine these with a modified CliNR protocol where stabilizer state preparation and verification are merged at the logical level and injection is implemented physically.
result: For $\ell = 20$ commuting logical operators on Q70 and Q102, the MECM protocol requires only 1.71 and 1.70 cat-state measurements per logical operator respectively, compared to 5.06 for the single-Pauli Viterbi protocol. Logical CliNR produces speedups of $4.2\times$ (Q70) and $5.0\times$ (Q102) for Toffoli gates, and $18.5\times$ (Q70) and $74.4\times$ (Q102) for random Clifford operators, versus gate-based Viterbi synthesis.
